SMTO-FIL-0062 — SMTO lost track of a file inside the compressed file

GUID: 97cbba80-c7dc-5d44-a189-a0f26dd7151c
Slug: attachment-archive-reference
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open a file inside the compressed file using a reference from an earlier look or from a different compressed file, so it didn't match. Nothing was read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to list what's inside the compressed file again, then open the file from that new list. Each entry is tied to the exact copy SMTO looked at, so a fresh list gives it a matching reference.
  2. If you attached a newer copy of the compressed file, tell SMTO which one to use. A changed copy gets new references, so ones from the older copy no longer match.
  3. Name the file you want using its full path exactly as it appears in SMTO's list. This helps SMTO pick the one entry you mean.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the file from inside the compressed file and uses its contents.

If it still fails

  • If SMTO still fails after listing the contents again, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The archive member_ref lacks this archive's exact inspection prefix ('am1:' plus the parent's SHA-256) and a numeric index; it is stale, from another archive, or a filename was used instead of a reference.

What this means

  • The member reference lacks the exact parent hash and index returned by inspection. Filenames alone are not member identities. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The member reference lacks the exact parent hash and index returned by inspection. Filenames alone are not member identities.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Call inspect_archive on the authorized parent context_id and pass a member_ref exactly as returned. References bind the parent's SHA-256 and member index, so they change whenever the archive changes; filenames are not accepted as references.
  • Inspect this authorized archive again and use an exact returned member reference.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The member reference matches the current authorized parent and a valid member index.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
